name: Nearby oppositely ordered fractions in the Farey sequence
description: construct() -> [[a,b],[c,d]], two reduced fractions in [0,1] with denominators <=1000, a/b<c/d, and (c-a)*(d-b)<0. Minimize their rank difference in the complete Farey sequence of order 1000, including 0/1 and 1/1. Every rank is recomputed exactly. The local finite search gives an upper certificate for the first possible ordering failure at order 1000. It corrects the feasibility draft's unrelated strictly monotone-run objective. The optimum is 252, found by scanning the complete Farey sequence of order 1000; this is a rediscovery task.

state_of_the_art.statement: The smallest rank difference between two oppositely ordered fractions in the Farey sequence of order 1000 is 252, i.e. f(1000) = 251 in the notation of Erdős Problem #1005. This comes from a full scan (scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py); OEIS A386893 tabulates f(n) for n <= 100, and the same scan agrees with it. Van Doorn proved (1/12 - o(1))n <= f(n) <= n/4 + O(1).
